title: Add Ninja Forms as a form provider (create-contact-form, plugin catalog, triggers, skill)
body:
## What
Add Ninja Forms as a first-class form provider in SD AI Agent, so the agent can create and manage forms on sites that use Ninja Forms (the CEF chapter template and every site cloned from it now use Ninja Forms only; WPForms is being retired there).

## Why
`sd-ai-agent/create-contact-form` only knows WPForms Lite, Contact Form 7 and an HTML fallback. On a Ninja Forms site it silently returns the dependency-free HTML block, so the CEF Setup Assistant cannot embed a real, notification-backed form.

## Files to modify
- `includes/Abilities/ContentAbilities.php`: add a Ninja Forms provider to `create_contact_form_result()` (Ninja Forms first, then WPForms when it is the active form plugin, then Contact Form 7, then the HTML block); add a `sd_ai_agent_contact_form_providers` filter so tests and sites can reorder or disable providers; update the ability description.
- `includes/Core/AbilityPluginRegistry.php`: add a `ninja-forms` catalog entry; reword the WPForms and Contact Form 7 entries (WPForms is supported when already active, not recommended for new sites).
- `includes/Automations/EventTriggerRegistry.php`: add a "Ninja Form Submitted" trigger on `ninja_forms_after_submission` (args `form_data`).
- `includes/Models/skills/contact-forms.md`: make Ninja Forms the recommended provider; document the `[ninja_form id="N"]` shortcode and detection.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/ContentAbilitiesTest.php`, `tests/SdAiAgent/Automations/EventTriggerRegistryTest.php`, `.wp-env.json` (install Ninja Forms in the test environment).

## Reference pattern
The existing `create_wpforms_form()` / `build_wpforms_form_data()` in `ContentAbilities.php` and the Gravity Forms / WPForms triggers in `EventTriggerRegistry.php`.

## Behaviour
- Provider id `ninja-forms`, shortcode `[ninja_form id="N"]`, shortcode block returned like the WPForms path.
- Form: Name, Email, Subject, Message, submit button; Ninja Forms' built-in honeypot stays on. Actions: save submission, email notification to the recipient (reply-to the submitter's email), success message.
- No `affected` post descriptor (Ninja Forms forms are not posts).

## Verification
- `pnpm run wp-env:start` then `pnpm run test:php` for the three test classes: provider selection, created form fields/actions/recipient, fallback to HTML when no provider is active, and the new trigger registration.
- `composer lint` (PHPCS and PHPStan) clean on the changed files.

title: Add-credit popup when SD AI credit runs out
body:
## Problem

Many users spend the $10 free SD AI credit and then stop. We walked through the current path from "credit ran out" to checkout with a scripted browser and found these problems:

- The chat only shows an inline notice. It promotes coupon `EARLY` ($200 free) and a review request, not adding credit.
- The notice button opens `#/settings`, which lands on **General**, not the account tab. The user has to find the "SD AI" tab themselves.
- On the account tab, **Redeem Coupon** is the primary button and **Add credits** is a secondary button in 4th position.
- After paying, nothing detects the new balance or resumes the request that failed.

## Expected

When credit runs out, a popup opens in the chat (main chat and floating widget). **Add credit** goes straight to checkout, the new balance is detected when the user returns to the tab, and **Continue my request** resends the failed message. A coupon field is available behind a quiet link, and the EARLY coupon is no longer advertised.

## Files

- `src/components/credit-upgrade-modal/{prompt,index}.js` (new): lazy host and popup.
- `src/store/slices/uiSlice.js`, `src/store/slices/jobSlice.js`: prompt state, opened when a job fails with `credit_exhausted`.
- `src/components/chat-messages/account-action-message.js`, `src/embed-widget/index.js`, `includes/Core/ActiveJobFailureDiagnostic.php`, `src/store/slices/active-job-failure-diagnostic.js`: notice copy and actions.
- `includes/Admin/{UnifiedAdminMenu,FloatingWidget}.php`: `accountPageUrl` and `canManageBilling` localized data.
- `src/settings-page/superdav-account-manager.js`: Add credits becomes the primary button.

## Verification

`pnpm run verify`, plus a Playwright walkthrough that simulates a `credit_exhausted` job on the local site.

title: fix: validate-block-content reports self-closing blocks as unclosed (false valid:false)
body:
## Observed `sd-ai-agent/validate-block-content` returns `valid: false` for correct block markup that contains self-closing blocks such as ``, `` or ``. It reports `invalidBlocks: 0`, `freeform_count: 0` and one warning: ```text Mismatched block comments: 35 opening vs 30 closing. Check for unclosed blocks. ``` Reproduced on 2026-11-18 against the sdaiagent.com footer template part (Ollie `footer-light` pattern, unmodified core markup): 35 openers, of which 5 are self-closing, and 30 closers, so the markup is balanced. Impact: `create_post` / `update_post` auto-run this validator, so the agent sees a false failure for any page, template or part that uses self-closing core blocks (site title, site logo, social links, navigation links, post title, spacer-free layouts with query blocks). It may then "repair" valid markup or give up. ## Cause `includes/Abilities/BlockAbilities.php` (around line 2465): ```php $opens = preg_match_all( '/`), which never have a matching ``. ## Expected Exclude self-closing block comments from `$opens`, for example by subtracting `preg_match_all( '/).)*?\/-->/s', $content )`, or by deriving balance from `parse_blocks()` output instead of regex counting. Balanced markup with self-closing blocks must return `valid: true` and no mismatch warning. Genuinely unclosed blocks must still warn. ## Files to modify - `includes/Abilities/BlockAbilities.php`: the opening/closing count before the `Mismatched block comments` warning. - The existing PHPUnit test class for `BlockAbilities` validation (find with `rg -ln "validate-block-content|Mismatched block comments" tests/`): add one case with self-closing blocks (valid) and one with a genuinely unclosed `` (still warns). ## Verification ```bash pnpm run test:php -- --filter=BlockAbilities pnpm run verify ``` Then, on any WordPress 7.0 site with the plugin active: ```bash wp eval 'var_dump( wp_get_ability( "sd-ai-agent/validate-block-content" )->execute( array( "content" => "\n\n\n

x

\n" ) )["valid"] );' ``` Expected output: `bool(true)`. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.189 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) ### Files Scope - `includes/Abilities/BlockAbilities.php` - `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/BlockAbilitiesTest.php`

title: feat: neutral, dismissible WordPress.org review request after real use (no incentive, no gating)
body:
## Goal

Ask active users for an honest WordPress.org review in a way that follows the plugin team's rules, so ratings grow from real use. The plugin has 2 ratings today; competitors show hundreds.

Rules this must follow (WordPress.org plugin team, "What's the deal with invalid reviews?", make.wordpress.org/plugins, 2022-06-15, updated 2025-01-23):

- A dismissible notice in the plugin's own admin screens is the recommended way to ask.
- No reward of any kind for a review (credits, coupons, features). A reward makes the review invalid and can get the plugin closed. Today the credit-exhausted notice pairs the EARLY $200 coupon with "We only ask that you please leave a review" (`src/components/chat-messages/account-action-message.js`, `src/embed-widget/index.js`, `includes/Core/ActiveJobFailureDiagnostic.php`). Draft PR #3007 (issue #3006) removes that pairing; merge it before or with this work, and keep any review ask out of credit or billing flows.
- No review gating: don't ask "are you happy?" first and send only happy users to WordPress.org.

## Behaviour

Show one neutral, dismissible notice only on SD AI Agent admin screens (the `AI Agent` menu pages, never the main Dashboard or other plugins' screens) when all of these are true:

1. The current user can `manage_options`.
2. The plugin was activated at least 7 days ago.
3. The site has at least 5 rows in `{$wpdb->prefix}sd_ai_agent_changes_log` (`includes/Core/Database.php` around line 188), meaning the agent has completed real work. If a better "completed task" signal exists, use it and say so in the PR.
4. The user hasn't dismissed it permanently and isn't inside a 30-day snooze.

Copy (no incentive, no sentiment question):

> Is SD AI Agent useful on this site? An honest review on WordPress.org helps other site owners decide, and tells us what to fix.
> [Write a review] [Maybe later] [Don't ask again]

- "Write a review" opens `https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/superdav-ai-agent/reviews/#new-post` in a new tab and dismisses permanently.
- "Maybe later" snoozes for 30 days (per-user meta).
- "Don't ask again" dismisses permanently (per-user meta).
- Dismiss actions are nonce-protected.

## Files

- New handler in `includes/Admin/`, modelled on `includes/Admin/ThirdPartyAbilityNoticeHandler.php` (nonce-protected dismiss URL, `is-dismissible` notice) and registered like the other notice handlers (see `includes/Admin/DefaultModelNoticeHandler.php` and `includes/Plugin.php`).
- Activation timestamp: reuse an existing activation option if one exists (`rg -n "activat" includes/Core includes/Bootstrap`); otherwise store one on activation.
- A PHPUnit test for the display conditions (each of the four conditions blocks the notice; all four met shows it) and for both dismiss actions.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run test:php -- --filter=ReviewRequest
pnpm run verify
rg -n -i "coupon|credit|EARLY" includes/Admin/*Review*   # must print nothing: no incentive in the notice
```

Manual: on a test site with 5+ change-log rows and the activation time set 8 days back, the notice appears on AI Agent > Chat and not on Dashboard; each button behaves as described.

title: Re-check spend cap before each provider call in AgentLoop::run_loop()
body:
## Problem

`BudgetManager::check_budget()` is only called at run entry (`includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:713` in `run()` and `:1024` in `resume_from_checkpoint()`). `run_loop()` and its follow-up/fallback provider calls (around `AgentLoop.php:2056`, `:2254`, `:2528`) do not re-check, so in pause mode a run that starts below the cap can cross it and keep spending.

Raised by CodeRabbit on PR #3013. The readme was narrowed to "new agent runs are blocked once a cap is reached" as an interim; fixing this lets the listing claim a stricter cap.

## Files to modify

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — call `BudgetManager::check_budget()` before each provider call in `run_loop()` and the follow-up/fallback calls; on `WP_Error`, stop and return it via the same exit path as the entry check.
- `includes/Core/BudgetManager.php` — reference only (`check_budget()` at line 47).

### Files Scope

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AgentLoopTest.php`

## Verification

- `pnpm run test:php -- --filter='AgentLoop|BudgetManager'` then the full `pnpm run test:php`.
- Manual: set a tiny daily cap in pause mode, start a multi-iteration run, confirm it stops with the budget `WP_Error` mid-run.

title: Enforce disabled tool_permissions on MCP tools/list and tools/call
body:
## Problem

The chat path refuses abilities whose `tool_permissions` entry is `disabled` (`includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:1417`, `:4610`). title: Add next_steps recovery guidance to failed ability responses
body:
## Summary

Failed ability calls return `{ error, code }` to the agent and nothing about what to do next. Only input-validation failures (`hint`, `example_arguments`) and repeated identical failures (`nudge`) carry recovery guidance. The remaining ~500 distinct `WP_Error` codes under `includes/` leave the model to guess, which drives retry loops with the same arguments.

Source: WP Product Talk, "Your Plugin's Next User Is an AI Agent" (John Turner, WP Vibe). Takeaway: every error should say how to self-correct, and success/error responses should point at the next step.

## Audit findings

- `rg -U -No "new WP_Error\(\s*'([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)'" includes --glob '!includes/Core/**'` yields 525 distinct literal codes, plus dynamic prefixes in `includes/Abilities/MessagingAbilities.php`.
- Code names follow stable conventions: `*_not_found` (42), `*_failed` (91), `*_invalid_*` (93), `*_missing*`/`*_empty_*`/`*_required` (~88), `*_forbidden`/permission (~16), `*_not_configured` (6), `*_unavailable` (10).
- Only `includes/Abilities/PublicChatSetupAbilities.php` exposed a `next_steps` field before this change.
- The single model-visible chokepoint is `includes/Core/AbilityFunctionResolver.php::execute_ability()`.

## Fix

- Add `includes/Core/AbilityErrorGuidance.php`: ordered code-pattern rules produce a bounded `next_steps` list. An ability may override with `new WP_Error( $code, $msg, array( 'next_steps' => array( ... ) ) )`. Only that key is read from error data; nothing else is copied into the model-visible payload.
- Wire it into the resolver's `WP_Error`, exception, tier-2 dispatch and static error paths. Payloads that already carry a validation `hint` are left unchanged.

## Verification

- `pnpm run test:php -- --filter='AbilityErrorGuidanceTest|AbilityFunctionResolverTest'`
- `rg -n "AbilityErrorGuidance" includes/ tests/`

## Follow-up (not in this issue)

- Add explicit `next_steps` to the highest-traffic abilities where the generic text is too vague (`includes/Abilities/WooCommerceAbilities.php`, `PostAbilities.php`, `ImageAbilities.php`).
- Surface next steps on successful responses (for example after create-form style calls).

title: Add ability-specific next_steps to high-traffic ability errors (posts, WooCommerce, images)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3020 / PR #3021. Failed ability calls now get default `next_steps` derived from the error-code name (`includes/Core/AbilityErrorGuidance.php`). Defaults are deliberately generic ("look up the correct identifier first"). For the highest-traffic abilities the model needs the *specific* recovery call, for example "call `sd-ai-agent/list-posts` to find the post ID". Add explicit steps there.

## How the override works

An ability returns steps in `WP_Error` data. `AbilityErrorGuidance::for_error()` reads only the `next_steps` key, trims each step to 300 characters and keeps at most 4:

```php
return new WP_Error(
	'ai_agent_post_not_found',
	__( 'Post not found.', 'superdav-ai-agent' ),
	array(
		'status'     => 404,
		'next_steps' => array(
			'Find the post ID with sd-ai-agent/list-posts (filter by title or post_type), then retry with that ID.',
		),
	)
);
```

Reference implementation for wording and tone: `includes/Abilities/PublicChatSetupAbilities.php::build_next_steps()`.

## Files to modify

Replace the generic default only where an ability-specific call exists. Verify each referenced ability name against its `register` call before using it (`rg -n "'sd-ai-agent/<name>'" includes/Abilities`); never reference an ability that does not exist.

- `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php`: `ai_agent_post_not_found` (5 sites), `ai_agent_empty_post_id` (4), `insufficient_capability` (5), `sd_ai_agent_status_change_confirmation_required`, `sd_ai_agent_scheduling_unsupported`, `sd_ai_agent_no_effective_post_updates`.
- `includes/Abilities/WooCommerceAbilities.php`: `sd_ai_agent_commerce_target_not_found`, `sd_ai_agent_commerce_prerequisite_changed`, `sd_ai_agent_commerce_target_required`, `sd_ai_agent_commerce_plan_operations_invalid`, `sd_ai_agent_commerce_vendor_prerequisite`.
- `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities.php`, `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/GenerateImageAbility.php`, `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php`: `uploads_disabled`, `no_results` (suggest a broader query or another source), `ai_client_unavailable` (configure a provider, do not retry), `no_image_provided`, `not_an_image`.

Out of scope: renaming any `sd-ai-agent` identifier (see root `AGENTS.md` "CANONICAL NAMING"), and changing error codes or HTTP statuses.

## Rules

- Steps are model-facing instructions in plain English, not translated user copy. Do not wrap them in `__()` unless the surrounding file already does so for model guidance.
- Never put secrets, file system paths or user data into steps.
- Keep it to 1 to 3 steps per error. Do not duplicate what the default already says.
- Do not touch the validation `hint` path in `AbilityFunctionResolver`.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run test:php -- --filter='AbilityFunctionResolverTest|AbilityErrorGuidanceTest|PostAbilities|WooCommerceAbilities|ImageAbilities'
pnpm run lint:php && composer phpstan
rg -n "'next_steps'" includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php includes/Abilities/WooCommerceAbilities.php includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities.php
```

Add one assertion per touched file (existing test class for that ability) that the failing call returns its specific step. Then run the full `pnpm run verify`; use a dedicated `WP_TESTS_DB_NAME` and `WP_PHPUNIT_CACHE_DIR` if other workers share the default test database.

title: Add next_steps to successful create/plan ability results
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3020 / PR #3021. Failed ability calls now carry `next_steps`. Successful calls do not, so after a create-style call the agent has to guess the logical next action. Source: WP Product Talk, "Your Plugin's Next User Is an AI Agent": "you've created the form, now you probably want to do this next".

## Constraints that shape the design

- Success results are returned unchanged by `includes/Core/AbilityFunctionResolver.php::execute_ability()` (`return new FunctionResponse( $function_id, $function_name, $result );`). Abilities validate output against their `output_schema()`, so a new `next_steps` key must be declared there or `validate_output()` rejects the result.
- Every success payload costs tokens on every call. Only add steps where there is a clear, non-obvious follow-up. Do not add generic "you can now..." text.
- Reference pattern: `includes/Abilities/PublicChatSetupAbilities.php` (`next_steps` is in its output schema at about line 128 and built by `build_next_steps()`).

## Scope (keep it small first)

Add `next_steps` (list of up to 3 short strings, model-facing, English) to the success result of a few abilities that create or change something and have an obvious follow-up. Candidates to evaluate in this order, and drop any where no real follow-up exists:

1. A create-post ability in `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php`: for a draft, suggest verifying the content and publishing only with explicit user intent. Do not suggest publishing automatically; status changes already require confirmation (`sd_ai_agent_status_change_confirmation_required`).
2. Image generation and upload in `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities.php` and `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/GenerateImageAbility.php`: suggest attaching the returned attachment ID to the post or block that needed it.
3. One WooCommerce planning ability in `includes/Abilities/WooCommerceAbilities.php` that returns a plan: suggest reviewing the plan with the user before applying it.

Decide per ability after reading its `output_schema()` and existing result shape. If fewer than two abilities qualify, say so in the PR and stop rather than padding.

## Rules

- Update each ability's `output_schema()` so the new key validates.
- Steps must not instruct the agent to perform destructive, publishing or payment actions without user confirmation.
- Never include secrets, paths or user data in steps.
- Do not change the resolver success path unless a shared helper is clearly cheaper than per-ability changes; if you do, keep the failure path in `AbilityErrorGuidance` unchanged.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm run test:php -- --filter='PostAbilities|ImageAbilities|WooCommerceAbilities|AbilityFunctionResolverTest'
rg -n "'next_steps'" includes/Abilities
pnpm run lint:php && composer phpstan
```

Add one assertion per touched ability that the success result contains `next_steps` and still passes output validation. Then run the full `pnpm run verify`; use a dedicated `WP_TESTS_DB_NAME` and `WP_PHPUNIT_CACHE_DIR` if other workers share the default test database.

### Files Scope

- `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php`
- `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/GenerateImageAbility.php`
- `includes/Abilities/WooCommerceAbilities.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/PostAbilitiesTest.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/AiImageAbilitiesTest.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/WooCommerceAbilitiesTest.php`
